name: JSRF Unleashed
subtitle: Jet Set Radio Future on iPhone and iPad
description: JSRF Unleashed: Jet Set Radio Future, statically recompiled to run natively -- not an emulator. You need your own copy of the game (the USA release); this source has the app only. Source code, the Mac and Linux builds and instructions: https://github.com/JuMatt/JetSetRadioFuture-Unleashed

apps.name: JSRF Unleashed
apps.subtitle: Jet Set Radio Future, natively
apps.localizedDescription:
Jet Set Radio Future, statically recompiled: the game's own code translated to native code and running on Metal -- not an emulator.

Bring your own game: the USA release of Jet Set Radio Future. After installing, open the app once, then copy the game into its folder in the Files app (On My iPhone > JSRF Unleashed): either the extracted folder with default.xbe in it, or the disc image (.iso), which the app unpacks itself.

A controller is the best way to play (Xbox, PlayStation, MFi and others); without one there are on-screen controls. Widescreen 16:9, or the whole screen on iPhone; saves are kept in the game's folder.

Experimental: plays on iPhone, but far less played than the Mac build. Bug reports with the log from the app's Logs folder are welcome on GitHub.

versions.localizedDescription: Vibration, as on the console: a controller vibrates as the game asks, and with the on-screen controls the iPhone itself. Turn it off in the settings.
A map selector: Go to a map in the settings takes you straight to any of the 14 maps, to skate it freely.
Photo mode now freezes the whole world: skaters, people, cars and spray cans hold still while you frame the shot.
Photo mode (the settings, or hold Back with a controller), and no more towers popping in in Skyscraper District.
The brake sparks and smoke now come every time, as on the console (the fix found by Miggas).
The camera on the right stick can now be set to tracking (in the settings): the right stick looks around while you keep going.
Widescreen: the HUD at the edges of the screen (16:9 and Fill the screen), and the boost's heat haze over the whole picture.
Faster where the game used to stall: entering an area, fades, and the work done for every drawing command -- six of the speed fixes spriteice found.
A hang where the picture stopped for good, now and then, while the game waited for room for its drawing commands is fixed.
The camera on the right stick turns smoothly, the sound chip runs a frame at a time as on the console, and a hang a few seconds into a level is fixed.

Shaders are built ahead from the first start, so the first visit to an area no longer stutters while they are made, and the sound no longer stutters with the picture. New: the right stick turns the camera (on by default; the settings turn it off).

Rails, rafters and walkways that were missing (Kibogaoka Hill, the Fortified Residential Zone among them) are drawn again: the game sends that scenery in batches longer than the renderer kept. The boost dash's haze no longer breaks up over shadows and glass, and graffiti, windows and signs flicker less against their walls in the distance.

Shadows: skaters cast their shadows on the ground, and buildings and bridges shade the streets -- and whoever skates through the shade. The game worked them out every frame, but its last step, the one that darkens the shadowed places, was never drawn.

Sharper in the distance: faraway buildings and windows no longer shimmer -- the game's own mipmaps are used now, with 16x anisotropic filtering. Anti-aliasing, SMAA and MSAA, in the settings (the gear button). Reflective glass, like Dogenzaka Hill's footbridge, reflects as on the console. Thanks to spriteice, whose fork had MSAA and anisotropic filtering first!

Smoother: when the game's threads take turns, the one giving way no longer pauses for a millisecond with nothing running in between (on a Mac, 8 slow frames instead of 34 in four minutes of 99th Street). And everything needed to build the game yourself, from your own disc, is now in the repository. Fixes found by spriteice -- thank you!

The graffiti you pick now shows in the picker and on the walls. Textures the game has finished with are let go, so video memory no longer grows at every area, and the Saves folder no longer shows as 10 GB in the Files app. Fixes found by spriteice -- thank you!

Less stutter: new textures appear about six times faster, so arriving in an area no longer freezes the game for a fifth of a second, and shaders are kept between sessions and built before the game needs them. No more grey spikes shooting across the screen from some objects.

The character select shows the skaters where they are: in its two preview windows they came out too big, too low and off to the right, under the rails they grinded and into the floor. A disc image is checked before it is unpacked, and files of another game or another build of it (the European or Japanese release, the Sega GT 2002 + JSRF combo disc) are named instead of crashing.

The robot at the future site of the Rokkaku Expo Stadium starts and fights, so chapter 5's Urban Battle can be finished: until now it hung out of reach and never moved. The Rokkaku robots make their sounds too, and two more of the game's missing functions are in.

The black city in the Skyscraper District and Pharaoh Park is fixed: the game's fog was emulated wrongly, which painted the scenery entirely in the fog colour. Areas with a coloured fog no longer come out as a flat wall of that colour, and distant buildings fade into the night or the haze as they should.

No more crash at the third tank in Chuo Street: the tanks' sound function and 26 more functions of the game that were missing are in now, and the sounds of 17 kinds of objects, the tanks among them, play for the first time. A call into code that is still missing no longer upsets the stack.

Fill the screen: a new choice in ⚙ › Picture widens the game to the whole iPhone screen. 16:9 stays the default, and the title screen stays 4:3. The picture is a new setting: if you had switched widescreen off, pick 4:3 again in ⚙ › Picture. Also a stability fix for long sessions, which the other versions already had.
First iPhone and iPad release (experimental): the Metal renderer, on-screen controls, controllers and keyboards, the game copied in through the Files app or unpacked from a disc image.
